Banks want to automatically block the accounts of Russians who deposit an amount higher than their monthly income through an ATM – they will have to justify the origin of the money with documents.

Sources in the banking sector claim that major banks have started testing stricter cash deposit verification. Algorithms will compare the deposited amount with the client's official income and their usual financial behavior. If a person earns 50 thousand rubles and then deposits 100 thousand in cash into the account, the transaction can automatically be flagged as high risk.

After such a signal, the bank can temporarily restrict some operations and request confirmation of the origin of the money. Purchase contracts, receipts, and other documents explaining the appearance of a large sum will be required. They particularly want to scrutinize cases where the cash amount significantly differs from the person's salary or previous transactions.

It will also become harder to bypass the system by splitting the amounts. According to sources, several deposits of 20-30 thousand rubles in a short period can be linked together by the algorithm and evaluated as one large operation. As a result, the checks may affect not only the gray market but also ordinary Russians who have kept money at home for years, received cash from relatives, or sold a car.

In Krasnodar supermarkets, there is already an option to pay with digital rubles, but according to regulations, the limit for digital rubles is 300 thousand rubles. You can never have more than this amount in your digital wallet. And in the event of the cancellation of cash and other forms of national currency, wages cannot exceed 300 thousand rubles.

Oh, and yes, the digital ruble will be voluntary, according to the Central Bank of Russia. Just like vaccines and the doomsday messenger.

📌 Threshold Signatures: Splitting Key Control Without Classic Multisig

Main Points
⏺ Threshold signatures let multiple participants jointly create one valid signature
⏺ The full private key doesn’t need to live in one place
⏺ This post explains why the model matters for wallets, custodians, and teams

1️⃣ Core Idea — a key is split into shares, and a required threshold must cooperate to sign.
2️⃣ How It Differs — on-chain, it may look like one normal signature; coordination happens under the hood.
3️⃣ Where It Helps — institutional custody, team wallets, exchanges, and smoother wallet UX.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — implementation complexity, participant coordination, lost key shares, and software trust.
5️⃣ Practical Check — know who holds shares, how recovery works, and what happens if one participant fails.

Final Thoughts

Threshold signatures hide key-management complexity behind one signature. Useful, but security still depends on the setup and participant discipline.

🔔 SpaceX stock falls as $60B Cursor deal closes 

‼️ SpaceX has completed its $60 billion stock-based acquisition of Anysphere, bringing the Cursor coding platform into its SpaceXAI business as SPCX shares fell during Friday trading. The closing came less than two months after SpaceX signed the merger agreement on June 16. Under its terms, the company valued Anysphere at an implied equity value of $60 billion and agreed to compensate its investors with SpaceX Class A common stock.

🔖 Cursor’s common and preferred shares outstanding immediately before the merger were automatically converted into rights to receive 389,289,254 SpaceX Class A shares, according to the filing.SpaceX based the exchange on the volume-weighted average closing price of its Class A shares over the seven consecutive trading days before the acquisition closed. Rather than setting one fixed share price when the agreement was signed, the structure tied the final share count to SPCX’s recent market value. 

🌐 Vested Cursor restricted stock units were separately converted into rights to receive 1,752,426 SpaceX Class A shares before applicable tax deductions. Holders will receive cash instead of fractional shares where the exchange calculation does not produce a whole share. Unvested awards will remain tied to future service and vesting requirements. According to the filing, SpaceX assumed the outstanding awards and converted them into about 29,128,326 restricted stock units linked to its Class A shares.

The Arbitrage Engine Is Already Running

Let's talk about that brand-new pool you just saw launch. How does it earn anything on day one? The answer is simple: Arbitrage.

The moment a pool goes live, its price can slightly differ from the prices on major centralized exchanges (CEX). Smart traders and automated bots, known as arbitrageurs, are constantly scanning for these tiny gaps. They buy where it’s cheap and sell where it’s dear.

This isn't theoretical volume. Even today, with only a handful of live pools on Gala Swap, millions of dollars in arbitrage volume are flowing through the platform daily. Every single one of those trades pays a fee to the liquidity provider (LP).

Shabbat Shalom from Galilee

Did you know that the message Yeshua came to deliver was hard to comprehend even for many of His followers?

When you grow up in a world that defines sin by its own rules and removes the need for repentance and a personal relationship with God, the message of salvation by grace through faith can be difficult - even offensive.

Why?

Because it requires us to admit that there is nothing within our own good works that can save us.

“For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.”
Ephesians 2:8-9

Religion has always tempted man to believe that human effort and good deeds can earn God’s attention, forgiveness, and acceptance. That same thinking had deeply affected many during the time of Yeshua.

But Yeshua came with a very different message.

At one point, many of His followers found His teaching too difficult to receive - particularly His message about the necessity of giving His body and shedding His blood.

“Therefore many of His disciples, when they heard this, said, ‘This is a hard saying; who can understand it?’”
John 6:60

In their minds, Messiah was supposed to reign - not die.

He was supposed to bring peace, prosperity, and the restoration of Israel - surely not die in humiliation on a Roman cross while Israel remained under harsh occupation, with another destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple soon to come, followed by an even longer exile.

Yeshua never forces anyone to believe. He even challenged His own disciples to decide whether they would stay or leave, as many others had already done.

“From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more. Then Yeshua said to the twelve, ‘Do you also want to go away?’”
John 6:66-67

Then came Peter’s great confession of faith - words that have resonated with me many times during difficult seasons throughout my life:

“Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
John 6:68-69

His message is clear - there is a price that had to be paid for our sins.

He gladly paid it.

There is no way around it.

Salvation cannot be understood without acknowledging why He came. He was born sinless, yet He died for us and rose again.

“But God demonstrates His own love toward us, in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Romans 5:8

Yes, the resurrection is the key - but without His death there would have been no resurrection.

You cannot believe in a resurrected Messiah without believing that He had to die - and understanding why He died.

It wasn’t the Jews who killed Yeshua.

It was all of us.

Our sins put Him there.

The verse that changed my life when I was not even 18 years old, contemplating taking my own life, was Isaiah 53:6:

“All we like sheep have gone astray;
We have turned, every one, to his own way;
And the Lord has laid on Him the iniquity of us all.”

Think about this - Isaiah wrote these words hundreds of years before Yeshua came and fulfilled them.

The cross was not an accident. It was not a failed plan. Long before Yeshua was born, God had already revealed through the prophet that Messiah would bear our sins.

Yeshua didn’t die accidentally.

He came to do the perfect will of the Father.

Hours before His death, He prayed:

“Father, if it is Your will, take this cup away from Me; nevertheless not My will, but Yours, be done.”
Luke 22:42

And hundreds of years before Yeshua fulfilled it, Isaiah had already written:

“But He was wounded for our transgressions,
He was bruised for our iniquities;
The chastisement for our peace was upon Him,
And by His stripes we are healed.”
Isaiah 53:5

So if you are down today, remember this - a price was paid for your salvation.

You are no longer on death row if you repent and believe.

“For whoever calls on the name of the Lord shall be saved.”
Romans 10:13

He isn’t a baby.

He isn’t a crucifix.

He is the resurrected Lord who is alive!

Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband called the tender “unacceptable and destructive.” He said E1 would cut through “the heart of Palestine,” and warned that Britain would not accept the destruction of the two-state solution.

He also accused British policy of blaming Israel alone while ignoring Palestinian extremism, and said that approach had contributed to antisemitism and attacks on Britain’s Jewish community. 

Britain treats E1 as occupied territory and a test of whether a Palestinian state remains geographically possible. Israel treats it as part of its historic homeland and cites the Balfour Declaration as evidence that Britain once accepted that claim.

London threatens sanctions. Jerusalem answers with the British Empire.

📣 EU to revise MiCA rules in 2027 amid US stablecoin push 

⚠️ European Union officials are preparing to revise the bloc’s MiCA crypto framework in 2027 as foreign stablecoin restrictions and faster U.S. rulemaking expose gaps in the existing regime. The planned revision would examine how MiCA treats stablecoins issued outside the European Union. Current requirements have prevented several foreign issuers from receiving authorization, limiting their access to regulated exchanges across the bloc.

💬 “Reopening the file seems unavoidable at this stage,” an unidentified European diplomat told Euronews.

🔗 The diplomat cited positions taken by European institutions, including the European Central Bank, along with changes in global regulation and digital-asset technology. No final proposal has been published. Any amendment would need to pass through the EU’s legislative process before taking effect. The consultation covers developments that have occurred since MiCA entered into application. Its deadline has been extended to Sept. 30, with crypto issuers, service providers, regulators, central banks and finance ministries invited to respond.
